We observe that fine-scale dynamical details are often encoded in this gap. By commuting these two operations, the fine-scale details removed during downsampling can be captured. Furthermore, we employ a memory module to store these fine-scale features along the trajectory and retrieve them during rollout, generating spatially adaptive corrections that enhance long-horizon fidelity. Empirical results across five systems demonstrate that CoMNO improves prediction accuracy and long-horizon rollout stability.

papers.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
papers.abstract: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.

papers.title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation
papers.abstract: Solar filaments are cool, dense chromospheric plasma structures held by magnetic field lines above polarity inversion lines. Their destabilization triggers coronal mass ejections and severe space weather hazards. Segmenting individual filaments from ground-based GONG H-alpha observations (2048 x 2048 pixels) is challenging due to low contrast, turbulent fibrils, delicate barb structures, and annotator boundary variance. In this technical report, we describe SolarFilNet-V4, a targeted segmentation framework developed for the MAGFiLO 1.0 benchmark (Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026). Our method couples a lightweight Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions (k=15) and dual-frequency feed-forward blocks (DFFN) to follow extended flux ropes while capturing thin central spines. A shallow full-resolution convolutional branch operating at 1024 x 1024 preserves high-frequency edge details and mitigates transformer downsampling. We train the network using multi-task supervision over masks, centerline spines, barb boundaries, and pixel-contrastive representations. At test time, we apply 8-fold dihedral test-time augmentation (D4), bilinearly upscale predictions to the native 2048 x 2048 grid, and apply an activity-adaptive post-processing routine that calibrates morphological joining parameters for quiet versus active solar disks. On the official benchmark, SolarFilNet-V4 achieves an out-of-fold validation Panoptic Quality of 0.4340 and a Public Leaderboard score of 0.380. The model contains 15.46M parameters and requires 224.34 GFLOPs per forward pass, reducing parameter count by 36.8% compared to standard ResNet-34 U-Net baselines.

papers.title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
papers.abstract: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet we prove, at leading order, a d-wave inverse-square law, 1.376 times the spin-wave amplitude, a clover-shaped entangled region, exact without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term, and that each spin's entanglement is entirely pairwise. Four qubits can test the d-wave signs at present error rates.

papers.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
papers.abstract: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known. For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, which include all qubit stabilizer codes of this kind, we determine when the bound holds and how far it can fail. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. If this number is less than twice the number of logical qudits, the bound holds, also for degenerate codes. If it is exactly twice that, the bound overstates the number of pairs by at most the length of the longest classical maximum distance separable (MDS) code of that dimension, minus the dimension. Codes carrying values and derivatives of polynomials on the projective line attain this maximum whenever the field size is at least that dimension and the MDS conjecture is known for it, which includes every prime and, by a recently announced result, every even field size. If the number is more than twice the number of logical qudits, the violation is bounded in terms of the lengths of classical codes of a given Singleton defect, and the bound is attained for one logical qudit. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant.

papers.title: Robust Measurements of the Cosmic Microwave Background Lensing Power Spectrum in the Presence of Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence
papers.abstract: Achieving the scientific potential of upcoming high-sensitivity cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization surveys requires lensing analyses that are robust to unmodeled distortions of the polarization field. One such possible distortion is anisotropic cosmic birefringence, a direction-dependent rotation of the linear polarization plane that may arise from parity-violating physics such as axion-like fields. We quantify the impact of both modeled and unmodeled anisotropic birefringence on the CMB lensing measurement in the Marginal Unbiased Score Expansion (MUSE) framework. Considering noise levels expected for current and future CMB surveys, we find that neglecting birefringence produces a positive bias in the lensing bandpowers that increases towards small angular scales. For a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum $L(L+1)C_L^{αα}/2π=10^{-5}\,{\rm rad}^2$, the positive fractional bias can reach $(10.1\pm1.1)\%$ of the lensing power at $1375<L<2000$. Jointly estimating lensing and birefringence in the MUSE framework recovers the input lensing bandpowers and birefringence amplitude without detectable bias across all tested configurations. The joint MUSE estimator also reduces the scatter of the recovered birefringence amplitude by factors of $1.6\pm0.2$ to $2.4\pm0.3$ relative to a joint quadratic estimator, with the largest gains in the highest signal-to-noise configurations. These results indicate that a joint-field reconstruction with MUSE can recover unbiased estimates of the lensing and birefringence power spectra while still improving precision relative to quadratic estimators.

papers.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
papers.abstract: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.

papers.title: Sounding the Black Box: Online Training of Embedded Neural Networks in Forward-Only Physical Simulators
papers.abstract: Hybrid physics-neural simulators embed neural networks in partial differential equation (PDE) solvers to model unresolved subgrid dynamics while preserving resolved physics and conservation laws. Because closure outputs feed back across time steps, single-step offline regression does not directly minimize multi-step rollout error, motivating online trajectory optimization. Solver backpropagation through time (BPTT) is the standard online solution when solver derivatives are available, yet many operational Fortran and C/C++ simulators expose only non-differentiable, forward-only interfaces. We introduce FORGE (Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation), an online framework that trains embedded networks from forward runs alone by decoupling exact network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. Stage I warms up the rollout via a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step along output-orthonormal weight directions, canceling multi-layer feature drift via a final-layer correction. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields to fit a gain-bounded causal linear response operator across rollout steps, solves for regularized target outputs, and updates all weights via network backpropagation. Across five 2D and 3D benchmarks spanning phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation, FORGE outperforms gradient-free, reinforcement-learning, and emulator-based baselines, cutting coarse-solver test mean squared error (MSE) by 50%-96% in 2D and 70% in 3D, outperforming the strongest forward-only baseline by 16%-69%, and recovering 88%-98% of Solver BPTT's gains. Code is available at https://github.com/ChiyodaMomo01/FORGE.

papers.title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
papers.abstract: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times Σ$ solutions for $Σ$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions. For solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ gauge group for which a complete truncation ansatz of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $S^4$ is known, we also uplift the solutions to eleven dimensions and compute the holographic central charge of the dual four-dimensional $N=1$ SCFT with $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetry.

papers.title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
papers.abstract: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.

papers.title: Classical phase space distributions for quantum states in cosmology: General states, operator ordering and the geometry of fading non-commutativity
papers.abstract: In earlier work with Ashtekar and Kesavan we showed that, for linear fields in any FLRW background, the vacuum defines a probability distribution $ρ_o$ on the classical phase space whose moments are exactly the Weyl-ordered $n$-point functions. We extend that analysis in four directions. First, for an arbitrary state $Ψ$ we give an explicit formula, in the Bargmann representation, for the distribution $ρ_Ψ$ that reproduces all Weyl-ordered expectation values. For pure states it is non-negative precisely for coherent and squeezed states, each the Gaussian of a compatible Kähler metric, and the Gaussian smoothing needed to make it positive is either zero or the full coherent-state width. Second, for linear observables every operator ordering differs from the Weyl ordering by explicit products of $c$-number commutators. Third, for two linear observables in a pure Gaussian state, the classical correlation coefficient, the ratio of commutator to anticommutator and the squeezing are functions of a single angle between their Hamiltonian vector fields; this bounds the departure of arbitrarily ordered $n$-point functions from the moments of $ρ$. Fourth, for fields in FLRW the equality holds at arbitrary, possibly different, times and for every homogeneous isotropic quasi-free state. In de Sitter the non-commutative corrections fall as $e^{-N}$ for field and momentum and as $e^{-3N}/3$ for the field at two times. For the state inherited from inflation they stay suppressed in the radiation era, by the inverse occupation number, except near the nodes of the mode functions. The same squeezing entangles the modes $\pm\vec k$ relative to the radiation-era vacuum and makes displaced-parity measurements violate Bell inequalities, so the positive distribution describes a specified family of observables, not all measurements.

papers.title: TQ-HQNet: A Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for Cross-Domain Learning on Heterogeneous Data
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum neural networks are a promising direction for noisy intermediate-scale quantum computing, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by poor trainability, rigid circuit design, and weak robustness across heterogeneous real-world tasks. This paper proposes TQ-HQNet, a Trainability-Aware and Qubit-Efficient Hybrid Quantum Neural Network for cross-domain learning on heterogeneous data. The proposed framework combines three mechanisms: 1) adaptive latent compression to map domain-specific features into qubit-compatible representations, 2) trainability-aware search over compact variational circuit candidates, and 3) hybrid fusion of multiple shallow quantum experts to improve robustness without increasing qubit cost excessively. TQ-HQNet is evaluated on four public datasets spanning neurological screening, phishing detection, financial direction prediction, and DNA sequence classification. Across all domains, the proposed model consistently improves over a fixed hybrid quantum baseline, with balanced-accuracy gains of +0.280, +0.170, +0.071, and +0.060, respectively. Ablation and sensitivity studies confirm that gains arise from trainability-aware compact circuit selection and expert fusion, not circuit scaling. Although classical baselines outperform on some tasks, fixed-split results show consistent improvements over the fixed hybrid reference. These analyses support the practical role of compact selection and fusion, with repeated-split and hardware-aware studies left for future work.

papers.title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
papers.abstract: We describe an architecture and workflow for learning and generalizing the syntax and parameters of holographic quantum circuits (HQCs), which are natural quantum circuit analogs of classical tensor networks. An HQC uses mid-circuit measurements and resets on a small subset of "physical" qubits whose measurement outcomes become correlated through coupling with a register of persistent "ancilla" qubits, analogous to the physical and bond indices of a tensor network. Hence, an HQC with fixed qubit resources can efficiently generate samples from a large quantum state, and adding qubits to the HQC ansatz has the effect of exponentially increasing the effective bond dimension. Our machine learning approach provides mechanisms for harnessing both features of HQCs by extrapolating the syntax (e.g., a sequence of gates, measurements, and resets) and parameters (e.g., the angles appearing in single-qubit rotations) from a dataset of HQCs to longer or more expressive HQCs. We demonstrate the methodology and its performance on an analytically solvable dataset formed by a vector-valued generalization of the W-state. Finally, we provide an outlook for usage of the methodology for scaling the effective bond dimensions of HQCs in quantum simulation.

papers.title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
papers.abstract: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.

papers.title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
papers.abstract: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $Λ_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.

papers.title: Thermodynamic constraints on warm inflation with the Standard Model
papers.abstract: In warm inflation with the Standard Model (SM), an axion-like inflaton dissipates energy into the plasma through QCD sphaleron transitions. Current predictions assume a friction linear in the bias, defined as the free energy released per transition in units of the temperature. The friction, however, has only been simulated at moderate biases in pure SU(2) gauge theory. We show that, during slow roll, energy conservation, the axial anomaly and thermodynamics relate the bias to the quark chemical potentials generated by the transitions, independently of the form of the friction and of the reaction network in the plasma. A bias within the simulated range requires chemical potentials a few times the temperature, which typically lead to Higgs condensation. Conversely, small chemical potentials imply a large bias and, unless the dissipation is very weak, a temperature far above the axion decay constant, which requires a cutoff of the effective description above that temperature. We illustrate that deviations from linearity beyond the simulated range can change the inflationary dynamics qualitatively, so that reliable predictions require a real-time computation of the friction and the noise in QCD at large bias. With high-scale lepton-number violation, the quark chemical potentials also source a $B-L$ asymmetry that exceeds the observed value by many orders of magnitude already during inflation. Finally, we show that the same relation between the bias and the chemical potentials holds for derivative couplings of the inflaton to SM currents. Unless the dissipation is very weak, warm inflation driven by such couplings therefore requires either a temperature far above the decay constant or chemical potentials that typically lead to Higgs condensation.

papers.title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
papers.abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

papers.title: Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology
papers.abstract: We propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on General Relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. The model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial Misner--Sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to Einstein's equations. Going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. Our Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology (AFIC) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. The extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. Rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. This mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.

papers.title: Topological Phase Transition of $ F_{α}{}^{γ} F^{αβ} F_{β}{}^{η} \ F^{λμ} R_{γηλμ} $ AdS Black Holes
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic criticality and topological properties of four-dimensional charged anti-de Sitter black holes in the presence of a nonminimal electromagnetic-curvature interaction of the form \(F_α{}^γF^{αβ}F_β{}^ηF^{λμ}R_{γηλμ}\). Treating the coupling perturbatively to first order, we construct the corrected black hole solutions and derive their thermodynamic quantities in the extended phase space. Conventional critical behavior is examined through the criticality conditions for the Hawking temperature in both canonical and grand canonical ensembles. We then use thermodynamic topology to investigate the global structure of equilibrium configurations and its dependence on the thermodynamic parameters. In the canonical ensemble, two distinct regimes emerge: a noncritical region characterized by a total winding number \(W=+1\), and a critical region with \(W=0\). In the grand canonical ensemble, three distinct regimes are identified according to the electric potential. Interestingly, the low- and intermediate-potential regions share the same topological number, \(W=+1\), although conventional critical points occur only in the intermediate-potential region. The high-potential region, by contrast, is characterized by \(W=0\) and exhibits no conventional critical behavior. Our findings show that thermodynamic topology provides a global characterization of equilibrium configurations that complements conventional temperature-based criticality analysis, and that the global winding number alone does not uniquely determine the existence of conventional critical points.

papers.title: A spin chain as a deformed conformal field theory: an ODE/IM approach
papers.abstract: The ODE/IM correspondence relates ordinary differential equations to integrable quantum field theories in the continuum. We ask whether it extends to integrable spin chains of finite length $N$. We analyse the twisted XXZ chain at a special anisotropy and twist, focusing on states in its Lee--Yang scaling sector. Their finite-size corrections are expected to come from the Lee--Yang conformal field theory deformed by irrelevant operators, and with the help of the ODE/IM correspondence we make this deformation explicit for the energy and the local conserved charges. Near each of the two edges of the distribution of the Bethe roots, the chain behaves as one chirality of the Lee--Yang theory in a generalised Gibbs ensemble, whose chemical potentials depend on $N$. The ODE/IM correspondence describes each of these ensembles by a cubic oscillator, whose coefficients we determine as series in $1/N$. The two chiralities are not independent: finite-size effects couple them, so that the charges of each shift the chemical potentials of the other. This turns out to be a generalised $T\bar T$-type interaction. Solving this coupling self-consistently, we obtain the energy and the local conserved charges of the chain as series in $1/N$, with no free parameters. We verify these series against the Bethe ansatz, for the ground state and for an excited state.

papers.title: Flat Space Entanglement from Wedge Holography
papers.abstract: We study holographic entanglement entropy in three-dimensional flat space by combining wedge holography with a controlled flat limit of AdS end-of-the-world branes. The limit takes a wedge of AdS$_4$ bounded by two AdS$_3$ branes to a Randall-Sundrum-like configuration of two flat branes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval in the two-dimensional corner CFT becomes that of an interval at null infinity of the branes. The result has the functional form of the entanglement entropy of a two-dimensional Carrollian CFT, the proposed holographic dual of gravity in asymptotically flat three-dimensional spacetimes. However, the inferred central charges yield $c_M=0$ and $c_L\to\infty$ in the flat limit. Adding a gravitational Chern-Simons term produces a $c_M$-like contribution, but we still find $c_L\to\infty$ and $c_M\to0$ in this limit. Moreover, the corresponding extremal surfaces do not approach the swing surfaces proposed by Song and collaborators. Instead, they collapse onto null rays along null infinity. We argue that both features are generic for flat limits of AdS/CFT. They follow from entanglement entropy being a property of the domain of dependence and from the equality of causal and entanglement wedges for intervals in the vacuum.

papers.title: Dark vector meson effects on composite dark matter
papers.abstract: We extend previous studies of $\mathcal{G}$-parity-odd dark pion dark matter in a QCD-like $\mathrm{SU}(N_c)$ gauge theory with electroweakly interacting dark quarks to include the effects of $ρ$ mesons. We show that vector mesons can substantially affect relic abundance calculations through resonant enhancement, significantly affecting the conditions required to reproduce the observed relic abundance. Electroweak interactions further induce mixing between the dark $ρ$ mesons and Standard Model gauge bosons, opening new decay channels for the dark $ρ$ and modifying the effective interactions of the dark pions. We recast existing ATLAS and CMS searches to constrain the model, and perform a collider phenomenology study targeting the future FCC-hh and muon colliders, focusing on the resonant enhancement of cross sections in the $e^+e^-$, $μ^+μ^-$, and $W^+W^-$ final states for the latter. We show that the FCC-hh could probe $ρ$ mesons whose mass is up to 40 TeV.

papers.title: Bootstrapping two-loop $β$-functions for bosonic and heterotic strings
papers.abstract: Beyond one loop, $β$-functions of non-linear $σ$-models are hard to compute directly. We obtain them instead as a gradient flow of the low-energy effective action, whose coupling-space metric is fixed exclusively by symmetry. This gives a two-parameter family of O$(d,d)$-covariant, two-loop $β$-functions that covers the bosonic and heterotic string at once. Because only symmetry enters, the method opens a route to higher loops. As an application, we derive the two-loop RG flow of the integrable $η$- and $λ$-deformations; for the heterotic string, the correction is half of the bosonic one.

papers.title: Discovering Warped Extra Dimensions at Next Generation Dark Matter Detectors
papers.abstract: The coming years will see what could be the final push in the search for WIMP dark matter (DM), with direct detection reaching into the neutrino fog and indirect detection reaching TeV-scale thermal relics. We study a class of models that these experiments could discover: DM emerging from a warped extra dimension. In the IR, these scenarios appear generically as a $Z'$-type portal. We show that DM with electroweak couplings and TeV scale masses remains viable and discoverable within such a bottom-up context. However, the models require a 20\% tuning between the DM and $Z'$ masses, a tuning that is relaxed if the DM and $Z'$ are strongly coupled and heavier ($\sim$$10$ TeV). In fact, it is the strongly-coupled $Z'$-type portal which is UV-completed by the framework of a warped extra-dimensional Grand Unified Theory (GUT), where DM stability is a spin-off of suppressing proton decay, resulting in a $\sim$$10$ TeV Kaluza-Klein (KK) scale. We identify a variant of this framework where all gauge fields except a baryon-number gauge boson have suppressed couplings to the DM; this model significantly suppresses the direct detection rate, but it remains discoverable through indirect detection. Further, to address the little hierarchy problem associated with $\sim$$10$ TeV KK scale, inspired by the Super-Composite Higgs, we augment our extra-dimensional GUT setup with supersymmetry. We show that this model also possesses a DM candidate, now with a weakly-coupled and $\sim$${\rm TeV}$ mass $Z'$ mediator. In all cases, a near-term discovery remains possible, for instance with the now online Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO), suggesting that our first hint of extra dimensions could emerge from the high-energy sky.

papers.title: Enhanced spatial resolution and performance for N-body simulation of self-interacting dark matter
papers.abstract: Studying the implications of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) on astrophysical objects often requires simulations. N-body simulations are a standard tool but face a few challenges. One is resolving the mean free path in gravothermally collapsing halos. This is necessary to obtain accurate results and is achieved in state-of-the-art simulations by increasing the number of resolution elements. I aim to formulate a numerical scheme that gives an enhanced spatial resolution compared to those methods and allows increasing the resolution without changing the number of resolution elements. The novel scheme that I present is formulated by discarding the classic approach of using kernel functions and computing interaction probabilities. Instead, pairs of particles always interact if their distance is below a specific threshold. Importantly, this distance threshold depends on their relative velocity and the size of the time step. This new formulation no longer requires some of the computations in state-of-the-art schemes and thus helps to increase the performance. Through a variety of test problems with known solutions, I study the accuracy of the new scheme and demonstrate its advantages over state-of-the-art SIDM formulations. Notably, the scheme reduced the computational costs, making the SIDM computations typically much cheaper than gravity. As a consequence, a typical SIDM simulation of isotropic scattering requires only a few percent of its total computational cost for the self-interactions. In conclusion, the new scheme presents an improvement over previous schemes and helps to address current challenges. Besides the enhanced performance, it allows us to achieve a higher accuracy when simulating gravothermally collapsing SIDM halos.

papers.title: Massive de Sitter correlators at one loop
papers.abstract: Fermions and massive fields charged under an unbroken symmetry couple to the inflaton only in pairs, so their signals in primordial correlators begin at one loop. Templates for these signals are mostly late-time estimates. Starting from a representation of massive de Sitter correlators as finite Mellin-Barnes integrals, we compute the exact squeezed coefficients of these signals and their corrections away from the squeezed limit. The leading coefficient factorizes into a hard part and a soft vertex. Late-time estimates treat the hard part exactly but approximate the soft vertex by its late-time limit, whereas we compute both exactly. Without a chemical potential, the exact coefficient differs from the late-time one by a universal factor that depends only on the masses in the loop and the coupling at the soft vertex. For the heavy Standard Model loops, the exact signals are ten to thirty times larger than their late-time estimates. With a chemical potential, the ratio depends on the model, and at our benchmarks it reaches a factor of thirty for helical vectors and about a hundred for the fermion triangle, where we agree with recent exact results. Away from the squeezed limit the leading term soon fails, mainly through a drift in the phase of the oscillation, which we derive for scalar and fermion loops.

papers.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
papers.abstract: We perform the complete light-cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $κ$-symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which in its turn is required to be nonvanaishing and nontrivial in this limit. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

papers.title: Global $C^{2,α}$ Estimates for Complex $k$-Hessian Equations on Kähler Manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove an a priori $C^{2,α}$ estimate for classical admissible solutions of the complex $k$-Hessian equation on a compact Kähler manifold with a positive $C^α$ right-hand side.

papers.title: Conservative tidal effects to third post-Minkowskian order in scalar-tensor theories
papers.abstract: Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order. We retain the full velocity dependence at linear order in the tidal response coefficients. The calculation covers the scalar dipole and quadrupole and the electric, magnetic, and mixed quadrupoles and octupoles. Among them, the scalar dipole enters the dynamics already at third post-Newtonian (3PN) order, two orders before the gravitational quadrupole. At 3PM, the tidal correction to the angle also depends on the first scalar derivatives of the responses and contains terms linear in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. The results reproduce the general-relativistic tidal angle and the post-Newtonian tidal dynamics through 5PN, and a test-body calculation confirms their leading order in the mass ratio, including the Gauss-Bonnet terms for a companion with vanishing sensitivity.

papers.title: Gray II, Kähler Nullity and Ricci Flow on Generalized Flag Manifolds with Two Isotropy Summands
papers.abstract: We investigate Gray's second curvature identity, Kähler nullity, and homogeneous Ricci flow on generalized flag manifolds with two isotropy summands. We prove that every invariant metric satisfies Gray's second identity for both invariant almost complex structures. For the non-integrable structure, the Kähler nullity is trivial except at a distinguished metric ratio, where it coincides with the vertical distribution of a homogeneous fibration. This distribution is integrable and has totally geodesic leaves. For the integrable structure, the Kähler nullity exhibits a different behavior and need not be integrable away from the Kähler locus. Finally, we reduce the normalized homogeneous Ricci flow to an autonomous equation for the ratio of the metric parameters. The resulting dynamics identify two invariant Einstein directions and show that the Kähler--Einstein direction is attracting, while the other is repelling.

papers.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables $(ζ_1,ζ_2)$ built on the superalgebra $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ associated with the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli-Kyemba, the two dilation parameters $φ_1(p,q)$ and $φ_2(p,q)$ being meromorphic functions of two variables evaluated at $(p,q)$. The graded super-Fock space splits into four sectors: bosonic, $φ_1-$fermionic, $φ_2-$fermionic and bi-fermionic. In each of them we establish the diagonal representation of the density operator by means of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$derivative, angular integration and Berezin integration, and we give a unified compact form in terms of sectorial parametric functions. The total density operator is obtained in explicit form as the sum of the four sectorial contributions, and can be read as a mixture of the four sectors. We define the sectorial reproducing kernels, obtained from the resolution of the identity, we compute the matrix elements of the density operator in the super-coherent state basis, and we prove the hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties of the kernels, together with the series expansion of their diagonal values. An integral formulation relates the density operator, its density function and the reproducing kernel, the latter being the function associated with the identity operator. Berezin quantization in the bosonic sector yields the quantized operators associated with $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|^2$, $z^2$ and $\bar z^2$ and their mean values; the dispersions of the super-position and super-momentum operators show that the super-coherent states are intelligent states.

papers.title: Two-Dimensional Local Smoothing in Noncommutative Spaces and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing for planar half-waves with coefficients in a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $M$. For $N\ge2$ and $P_N=ψ(|D|/N)$ with $ψ\in C_c^\infty((1/2,2))$, we obtain $\|e^{it|D|}P_N f\|_{L^4([1,2]\times\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}\le C_ψ\sqrt{\log(2+N)}\|f\|_{L^4(\mathbb{R}^2;L^4(M))}$ uniformly in $M$ and its trace. Pairing the Dirichlet energies for $M$ and its opposite algebra cancels a determinant contribution that can have either sign. At $p=4$, summation over frequency annuli gives local smoothing for every Sobolev order $s>0$. Interpolating the annular estimates before summation gives spacetime $L^p$ bounds for $2\le p\le\infty$ and Sobolev orders $s>σ(p)=\max\{0,1/2-2/p\}$, as well as logarithmically weighted bounds at $s=σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$. The finite-$p$ bounds transfer to quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes, answering the question of Hong, Lai and Wang about the range $s>σ(p)$ for $2<p<\infty$ on generalized Moyal planes. For $1<p<\infty$ and complex $α$ with $\operatorname{Re}α>\max\{2/p-1,1/p-1/2,-1/p\}$, we prove maximal inequalities over all radii for generalized circular means on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes. For an action $β$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ on $M$ by normal trace-preserving $*$-automorphisms with norm-continuous $L^p$ orbits, the orbit mean $A_{t,β}^αx$ converges bilaterally almost uniformly to $πx/Γ(1+α)$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $x\in L^p(M)$. We also obtain estimates for truncated cone multipliers on three-dimensional Euclidean and quantum Euclidean spaces, and full-radius row and column bounds for Stein's square function on the plane, quantum tori and generalized Moyal planes.

papers.title: Non-invertible Duality Defects in Four-Dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Lattice Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We consider four-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ lattice gauge theories with generalized plaquette actions. These theories are known to exhibit dualities. We construct topological interfaces implementing these dualities by assigning a weight to each building block and proving topological invariance. At self-dual couplings, these interfaces become duality defects representing non-invertible symmetries. We also study center symmetry defects and their junctions with the duality interfaces and derive several crossing relations.

papers.title: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form $A(f_i)^*A(f_i)$, where $A(f)$ is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the $(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m}$ are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a bosonic Fock space, we derive the joint moment generating functional and the unique joint probability distribution for the observables $(A(f_i)^*A(f_i))_{i=1,\dots,m}$. As an application of these results, we construct a model of a Bell inequality test within quantum field theory using a recently developed coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements. We show that our Bell test model can violate the CHSH inequality, approaching Tsirelson's bound for maximally entangled states in the limit where vacuum effects are perfectly rejected. These results show that the state update rules derived in the Fewster-Verch framework are compatible with strongly quantum correlations. They also support a viewpoint in which state updates should be understood in relation to available information.

papers.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(φ)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $β$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $σ$, $ζ$, and $δ$, and vector fields $ω$ and $ρ$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^μ$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids interact only through gravity and are treated within a two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff formalism. We examine the resulting mass-radius relation and tidal deformability, along with the gravitational redshift, to investigate the effects of DM on neutron star structure and observable properties. The inclusion of $U_{\text{cut}}(φ)$ stiffens the EOS, whereas increasing the DM fraction generally softens the EOS and modifies the mass-radius relation, tidal deformability, and gravitational redshift. The magnitude and nature of these modifications depend on the DM particle mass and mediator interactions, which determine whether the resulting configurations exhibit compact DM cores or extended DM halos.

papers.title: Morita equivalence classification for irrational noncommutative solenoids
papers.abstract: Given a prime integer $p$, we define a $p$-angle to be an element of the $p$-solenoid ${\mathcal S}_p$ or equivalently an element of $\mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{Q}_p$ modulo $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$. Noncommutative $p$-solenoids, or equivalently $p$-rotation algebras, are $C^*$-algebras defined by a $p$-angle in the same way as non-commutative tori or usual rotation algebras are defined by an angle. We give a complete classification, in terms of their $p$-angles and in the irrational case, of these $C^*$-algebras up to strong Morita equivalence, but also the associated groupoids up to Morita equivalence; more precisely, we obtain the following classification result: two irrational $p$-angles define strong Morita equivalent noncommutative solenoids if and only if they define isomorphic dimension groups if and only if they are congruent modulo $GL_2(\mathbb{Z}[1/p])$ if and only if they define Morita equivalent groupoids. This generalises, with a different proof, the classification up to isomorphism, previously obtained by Latrémolière and Packer. We also give a geometrical construction of projective $C^*$-modules in terms of proper $G$-spaces which exhaust the dimension group up to a shift and implement all relevant Morita equivalences by groupoid equivalences.

papers.title: A decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels and its application to Williamson's diagonal form
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a decomposition of Hamiltonian matrices with symplectic kernels, which extends the main result in [K. D. Ikramov, On the Symplectic Eigenvalues of Positive Definite Matrices. Moscow Univ. Comput. Math. Cybern., 42(2018)1-4]. As an application, we present another proof of Williamson's diagonal form for positive-semidefinite matrices with symplectic kernels.

papers.title: On the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on a product with a torus
papers.abstract: We prove that if $N$ is a closed smooth manifold admitting a Riemannian metric of negative sectional curvature and $T^k$ is the $k$-dimensional torus, then there is a retraction from the moduli space of nonpositively curved Riemannian metrics on $T^k\times N$ onto the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$. As an application, we combine our retraction with Tuschmann and Wiemeler's work on the rational topology of the moduli space of flat metrics on $T^k$ to deduce that the moduli space of nonpositively curved metrics on $T^k\times N$ has nontrivial higher rational homotopy and cohomology groups when $k\geq5$.

papers.title: $μ$- and $q$-extension of special functions in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: Analytic calculations up to single-scale quantities in perturbative quantum field theory result into special numbers and functions, which are generalizations as iterative integrals over special alphabets. In this way one obtains polylogarithms, Nielsen integrals, the iterated integrals over linear denominator terms, cyclotomic letters, letters induced by quadratic forms, and square-root valued letters. The inverse Mellin transform relates special nested sums to these quantities, which are harmonic sums, generalized harmonic sums, nested sums implied by quadratic forms, cyclotomic harmonic sums, and nested sums containing central binomials. We construct the $μ$- and $q$-extensions of all these special functions. They are expected to occur in loop calculations within $μ$- and $q$-extended quantum field theories via modified (anti)commutation relations. The $μ$-extended special functions are quite different form the corresponding $q$-extended functions. While in the former case one observes class-preservation characterized by the polynomial $μ$-parameter, except for the case of root-valued letters. In the latter case new higher transcendental functions are obtained.

papers.title: Semiclassical Weyl laws and noncommutative geometry on open manifolds with conformally cusp metrics
papers.abstract: We establish semiclassical Weyl laws on open Riemannian manifolds with conformally cusp metrics of finite volume. These metrics need not be complete, and even when complete they do not have bounded geometry. Moreover, the potentials are bounded, the discreteness of the spectrum being a consequence of the geometry rather than of a confining potential. Therefore, our results lie beyond the scope of recent semiclassical Weyl laws of Dai--Yan and Braverman. The semiclassical Weyl laws are established for fractional Schrödinger operators associated with Dirac operators, magnetic Laplacians, and Hodge Laplacians, under conditions of Moroianu and Golénia--Moroianu which ensure that these operators have discrete spectra. We also obtain extensions of Connes' integration formula for the same operators. In addition, we deal with a class of conformally cusp metrics of infinite volume, in which case the semiclassical Weyl laws and the integration formulas only involve the values at infinity. The results are obtained by applying the abstract semiclassical Weyl laws and integration formulas for spectral triples established in a previous paper.

papers.title: Finite-Time Singularities of the $L_β$-Gradient Flow in a Kähler Surface
papers.abstract: We study finite-time singularities of the $L_β$-gradient flow of closed symplectic surfaces in a compact Kähler surface, with $β> 0$ fixed. We derive the evolution equation for the second fundamental form and obtain a lower bound on the blow-up rate of its maximum squared norm. Combining this bound with a local curvature propagation estimate and the weighted monotonicity formula, we rule out Type I singularities.

papers.title: Inner derivations and automorphism groups of vertex operator algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra of CFT type. We prove that the zero mode map $V_1\to\operatorname{Der}(V)$, $h\mapsto h_0$, is an isomorphism of Lie algebras. We prove surjectivity using traces on finite sums of weight spaces and Li's module construction, and injectivity using the vacuum character of Zhu's algebra. It follows that $\operatorname{Inn}(V)$ is the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ and has finite index in $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$. Moreover, $\operatorname{dim}\operatorname{Aut}(V)=\dim V_1$, so $\operatorname{Aut}(V)$ is finite if and only if $V_1=0$.

papers.title: Orthosymplectic $K$-matrices in small dimensions
papers.abstract: Using elementary methods, we describe coideal subalgebras of quantum orthosymplectic algebras of small dimensions, classify the corresponding $K$-matrices and find explicitly the centralizers of these subalgebras in the vector representation. The main attention is paid to generators with a Cartan term. For them, at generic values of the parameters, we find the centralizers and all $K$-matrices and describe the decomposition of the vector representation over the coideal subalgebra. We find all special values of the parameters of two types and, at a generic point of each set of special values, describe the decomposition of the vector representation and all $K$-matrices. At special values of the first type the dimension of the centralizer grows. One hypersurface of such values is related to Cartan terms, and on it one of the generators is given by the same formula as in the quantum electrical algebra. At special values of the second type the dimension of the centralizer is the same, but nonzero nilpotent elements appear in it. The $K$-matrices on the sets of special values of the second type are obtained from those already found by substituting the condition, and there are no others. We describe the classical limit, including the limit of special values. We formulate an observation relating the admissibility of a Cartan term to the first homology of the classical subalgebra.

papers.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
papers.abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.

papers.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
papers.abstract: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.

papers.title: Autonomous quantum machine learning via Riemannian gradient-based optimization
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning models typically rely on repeated quantum measurements and classical optimization during training, making the quantum-to-classical information-extraction process a fundamental bottleneck for scalability. We propose a framework for autonomous self-training quantum machine learning, based on Riemannian gradient optimization, in which the optimization proceeds entirely within the quantum domain without requiring quantum measurements or classical feedback. We derive the Riemannian gradient update rules for a broad class of learning tasks and identify sufficient conditions under which the resulting training dynamics can be realized fully autonomously. Within this regime, we establish an exponential convergence guarantee, in the training iterations, for sufficiently small step sizes, and further analyze the training cost in terms of the growth of the circuit depth. Importantly, we further show that the trained model can automatically discover symmetries hidden in the training data without $\textit{a priori}$ specification. For the canonical examples of quantum phase classification and unitary learning with a hidden symmetry, our numerical study indicates that learning can be achieved at low circuit depths with only a few distinct training examples. Our results thus establish autonomous quantum machine learning as a promising paradigm that removes the classical optimization loop while retaining strong theoretical guarantees and practical performances.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Feature Representations and Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models for Generalizable Melt Pool Geometry Prediction
papers.abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning for Shear Wave Speed Estimation in MR Elastography
papers.abstract: Objective: Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is a non-invasive imaging technique for mapping biomechanical properties of in vivo tissue, including shear wave speed (SWS), but involves intrinsically slow data acquisition and an ill-posed wave inversion. Instead of relying on handcrafted image priors, we propose a data-driven approach jointly combining image reconstruction and MRE inversion for robust SWS estimation from undersampled k-space data. Methods: Our physics-informed reconstruction framework comprises two blocks: a model-based neural network (NN)-regularized reconstruction module and a phase-gradient inversion (k-MDEV) calculating SWS from the reconstructed images. Concatenating both blocks yields an end-to-end trainable method to estimate SWS directly from measured k-space data. We evaluated the method on retrospectively highly undersampled brain MRE data and compared it to a total variation (TV) minimization-based approach. We assessed the impact of end-to-end training (qualitative images and SWS maps as targets) versus pre-training (qualitative images as targets) and applied the method also to in vivo data. Results: Our approach significantly reduces NRMSE by 30% compared to TV. End-to-end training improves SWS estimation over separate image reconstruction and SWS calculation. Conclusion: Accurate SWS quantification is possible at acceleration factors up to 19. Our method significantly outperforms TV, highlighting the need for data-driven regularization in this challenging MR problem. Further, our approach successfully generalizes to in vivo data. Significance: We present the first end-to-end trainable MRE reconstruction method for estimating SWS maps directly from k-space. NN-based reconstruction can enable rapid stiffness mapping for dynamic studies, functional imaging, and real-time clinical feedback.

papers.title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries
papers.abstract: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes. This work introduces a method for visualizing and measuring ANN decision boundary geometry directly in the high-dimensional input space, avoiding distortions found with traditional projection-based techniques. We analyze boundary curvatures and distances in diverse inputs, architectures, and training methods. Boundary distances grow smoothly and slowly with consistent curvature as the size of the subspace increases, suggesting that decision boundaries are close to input samples within large, continuous subspaces. We also quantify how much boundary distances and curvatures reduce near dataset samples after adversarial training. Training methodology has a significantly stronger impact on boundary distance and curvature than architecture or test-set accuracy. These findings are contextualized within prior work, supporting or refuting several previously proposed theories of boundary behavior. Our analytically and empirically supported methodology lays the foundation for future studies to improve network interpretability and understanding.

papers.title: Flipping the Coins: Training Physical Simulators through Hard Switches
papers.abstract: Hybrid simulators embed learnable components such as neural networks in physical solvers and train them on reference trajectories. Many scientific solvers feature hard switches, such as a tripping power line, an igniting grid cell, or depolarizing brain tissue, where the loss exhibits discrete jumps across switch flips, leaving standard automatic differentiation to capture only its smooth part. Existing training paradigms face a fundamentally challenging trade-off, as gradient-based relaxations smooth the switches and introduce bias across jumps, whereas derivative-free methods treat the solver as a black box and discard path gradients of the continuous dynamics. Here we introduce EventFlip, which flips a near-threshold switch from a stored state, replays the original solver, and measures the loss difference between the two runs, in effect a finite difference across the switch. By perturbing every threshold with small Gaussian noise, we cast each switch as a stochastic binary decision and derive an unbiased gradient estimator that combines the continuous path gradient with a jump term constructed from these counterfactual rollouts. EventFlip-Rand optimizes this noise-averaged objective, whereas EventFlip-Hard operates on the deterministic hard-switch simulator used at deployment and provably targets the complete discontinuous loss. Under an identical forward evaluation budget, we benchmark EventFlip against twelve baselines across a power-grid cascade, a detonation wave, and cortical spreading depolarization, achieving the lowest error on every task and reducing the strongest baseline's error by factors of 1.5, 1.4, and 1.4, respectively.

papers.title: PowerFix: Physics-Guided Iterative Repair for LLM-Assisted Power Converter Design
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly being explored for automated engineering design. However, repairing power-converter designs that fail engineering validation remains challenging: the system must identify physical causes, locate responsible design variables, and resolve violations without compromising other constraints. We introduce PowerFix, a physics-guided iterative repair framework that converts validation failures into structured diagnoses and executable patches while preserving topology and design requirements. PowerDiagGraph links failed checks to possible physical causes and constrains repair routes. An LLM prioritizes these routes, while a deterministic compiler translates selected repairs into authorized field-level edits. Candidates are validated on isolated design copies and committed only after all required engineering checks pass; failed validation can guide replanning. On our constructed 96-task flyback repair benchmark, comprising injected single faults, coupled faults, and held-out natural failures from our design generator, PowerFix achieves 78.7% verified repair success rate (VRSR), compared with 30.1% for the strongest of three LLM baselines. Three additional replanning rounds increase VRSR to 88.4%. These offline results provide pilot-stage evidence within a simulation-based design workflow, with hardware prototype validation and transfer to a second converter topology as the next steps toward deployment.
